### 1. What the caller expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The caller states the target object, the timing, the boundary of the action and the mode of
authorisation without ambiguity:

- **Object.** "she needs to stop the chiller project at Kestrel Court" — a named building and a named
  scope. She volunteers the purchase order when asked: "Asked for the purchase order, she reads it
  out, PO-2026-0418."
- **Timing.** "She wants it settled on this call, today, rather than left open over the weekend."
- **Boundary of the action.** "she wants to know what stopping it is going to cost the company before
  anything else happens" — a figure, then the stop.
- **Mode of authorisation.** "She is clear that she will do the stopping herself, because it is her
  signature on the contract and she is not letting anyone else press that button for her, but she is
  content for the desk to work the figure out and to do whatever the contract says the office has to
  do on its own side." Two owners are therefore in play: the office-side write is the agent's, the
  stop itself is the caller's.
- **Ground.** "Asked why the work is being stopped, she says the board withdrew the capital budget for it."
- **Identity.** Name, company and phone volunteered; account number `650142` and tax-id last four
  `5518` only on request — "she volunteers neither of those unless she is asked".

The simulator only conveys needs and answers passively under if/else ("Asked about anything an owner
has no way of knowing from her side of the desk … she says the desk will have to look at that"). It
executes a user-owned tool only once the agent hands it over: "When the agent hands the authorisation
across to her she runs it herself and says it has gone through." It states no internal reference
number ("she knows no internal reference numbers at all") and pushes no step on the agent's behalf.

#### 4a. The storage charge to be raised on the project

Computation document: **`Computation of the Storage Charge on a Retrofit Project`**
(`how_a_storage_charge_is_computed_31afd118.json`). Its seven numbered quantities are: the storage
clock, the weeks in storage, the free period, the weekly storage rate, the weekly charge for the lot,
the weeks charged and the charge.

| Input | Value | Where it came from |
|---|---|---|
| day the clock runs from | **2026-06-01** | tier of `The Day from Which Storage Runs on a Retrofit Project` |
| day the charge is raised | 2026-06-18 | `frozen_time` |
| weeks in storage | **3** | 17 days; "a part week counting as a whole week" |
| free period | **2 weeks** | tier of `Free Storage Period Allowed on a Retrofit Project` |
| weekly storage rate | **USD 345 / week** | class 225 + tier of `Weekly Storage Rate by the Kind of Unit Held` |
| weekly charge for the lot | **USD 517.50 / week** | tier of `Weekly Charge for a Lot of Several Units in Storage` |
| weeks charged | **1** | 3 less 2 |
| **storage charge** | **USD 517.50** | 1 week at USD 517.50, rounded to the nearest cent |

Tier derivations, each with the query return that put the project on it:

- **Clock start.** `The Day from Which Storage Runs on a Retrofit Project`: "The equipment arrived
  before the day installation was booked to begin, and that booked day has already passed → the booked
  installation day, rather than the arrival day"; and "The first case requires both things at once: an
  arrival earlier than the booked day, and a booked day that is already in the past." Records: most
  recent stored delivery `DL-880656` / `DL-880655` arrived **2026-04-22**; `scheduled_start_date` is
  **2026-06-01**; the charge is raised 2026-06-18, so 2026-06-01 is in the past. Both limbs met → the
  clock runs from **2026-06-01**.
- **Weeks in storage.** Baseline step 2: "the whole weeks begun between the day the storage clock runs
  from and the day the charge is raised, a part week counting as a whole week", and its worked row "the
  1st → the 9th of the same month, days between 8, weeks in storage 2". 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-18 is 17
  days; 14 days close a second week and the 15th begins a third → **3 weeks**.
- **Free period.** `Free Storage Period Allowed on a Retrofit Project`: "Where an active maintenance
  agreement covers the building and a late fee has been raised on the project in those twelve months,
  the free period is **2 weeks**", and "The late fees counted are the late fee lines standing on this
  project's own billing record whose due day falls inside the twelve months before the charge; a single
  such line is enough". Records: the PMA at Kestrel Court is `status 'active'`, and the late-fee line
  `INV-40231402` is due 2026-04-18, inside the twelve months before 2026-06-18 → **2 weeks**.
  (This is the cross-product read: the agreement is read from the Preventive Maintenance Agreements
  holding record through `find_maintenance_agreements`, in the record's own words "active".)
- **Weekly storage rate.** `Weekly Storage Rate by the Kind of Unit Held`: "Where the lot standing in
  storage is a chiller, a boiler or a cooling tower … the weekly storage rate is the project's weekly
  storage charge together with the yard premium of **USD 120 per week**", and "The kind of unit read is
  the kind recorded on the most recent stored delivery on the project." The most recent stored delivery
  is a **chiller** (`equipment_type 'chiller'`, `stored_off_site 'stored'`, 2026-04-22). The project's
  weekly storage charge is the class figure: `Equipment Lead Times, Storage, Temporary Cooling and
  After-Hours Charges` gives the Energy Retrofit Project **USD 225 per week**. → 225 + 120 = **345**.
- **Weekly charge for the lot.** `Weekly Charge for a Lot of Several Units in Storage`: "Where two
  units stand in storage, the weekly charge for the lot is the weekly storage rate multiplied by 1.5,
  the two units sharing one bay", and "The number counted is the number of deliveries on the project
  recorded as stored because the site could not receive them." Records: two such deliveries
  (`DL-880655`, `DL-880656`) → 345 × 1.5 = **517.50**.

#### 4b. The settlement figure the stopped project is settled at

Computation document: **`Computation of the Settlement Figure on a Stopped Retrofit Project`**
(`settlement_figure_on_a_stopped_project_9308dafd.json`). Its parts are the stage fee, the equipment
value, the restocking charge, the billings counted and the settlement due:
"The settlement due is the stage fee plus the restocking charge plus the billings counted, less every
payment received and every credit issued on the project; that difference is rounded to the nearest
cent, and where it falls below zero the project is settled at zero."

| Part | Working | Figure |
|---|---|---|
| stage rate carried by the stage | Energy Retrofit Project, cancelled after equipment release | 25 per cent |
| portion of the stage fee taken | notice recorded after the booked installation day | 75 per cent |
| stage fee | 268000 × 25% × 75% | **USD 50250.00** |
| equipment share of the contract value | chiller | 65 per cent |
| equipment value | 268000 × 65% | **USD 174200.00** |
| restocking fee applied | class 20% + 10 percentage points | 30 per cent |
| restocking charge | 174200 × 30% | **USD 52260.00** |
| billings counted (deposit, mobilisation, progress, change order, storage, completion) | 67000.00 deposit + 517.50 storage | **USD 67517.50** |
| late fees carried into the settlement | one late fee line of 837.50, at 50 per cent | **USD 418.75** |
| payments received | one payment | USD 67000.00 |
| credits issued | none | USD 0.00 |
| **settlement due** | 50250.00 + 52260.00 + 67517.50 + 418.75 − 67000.00 − 0.00 | **USD 103446.25** |

Tier derivations, each with the query return that put the project on it:

- **Stage.** `The Stage a Stopped Retrofit Project Is Charged At`: "Where the project record carries the
  day the equipment order was released to the supplier and no day the crew mobilised, the stage fee is
  taken at the project's cancellation fee for a project stopped after the equipment was released", and
  the rule is "read from the dates the project record carries, and not from what the owner says the crew
  had or had not done." Records: `equipment_released_date '2026-02-20'`, `mobilization_date ''` →
  the after-release stage. `Cancellation Fee and Restocking Schedule` gives the Energy Retrofit Project
  **25** per cent in the "Cancelled after equipment release" column and **20** per cent restocking.
- **Notice relief.** `Relief on the Stage Fee Where Written Cancellation Notice Was Given`: "Where a
  confirmed written cancellation notice stands on the project record and it reached the office 30 days
  or fewer before that booked day, **or after it**, the stage fee is taken at three quarters of the rate
  the stage carries, that is at **75 per cent** of it"; its table's fifth row reads "yes | the notice came
  after the booked day | 75 per cent". Records: `cancellation_notice`, `outcome 'confirmed'`,
  `notice_date '2026-06-09'`, against `scheduled_start_date '2026-06-01'` → the notice is **after** the
  booked day → **75 per cent**.
- **Equipment share.** `Equipment Share of the Contract Value on a Retrofit Project`: "Where the equipment
  delivered on the project is a chiller, a boiler or a cooling tower, the equipment share of the contract
  value is **65 per cent**", and "The kind read is the kind of unit recorded on the most recent delivery
  on the project." The most recent delivery (2026-04-22) is `equipment_type 'chiller'` → **65 per cent**.
- **Restocking fee applied.** `Restocking Fee Applied on Equipment Returned from a Stopped Project`:
  "Where equipment on the project stands in storage and it arrived 30 days or more before the stop day,
  the restocking fee applied is the project's own restocking fee together with a further **10 percentage
  points**", counted "from the day the most recent stored delivery arrived to the stop day". 2026-04-22
  to 2026-06-18 is 57 days, which is 30 or more → 20 + 10 = **30 per cent**.
- **Late fees carried.** `Late Fees Carried into the Settlement of a Stopped Project`: "Where exactly one
  late fee has been raised on the project, the settlement carries the billings raised together with half
  the late fees raised on the project, that is 50 per cent of them", counted as "late fee lines standing
  on the project's billing record". Exactly one such line stands (`INV-40231402`, 837.50) → **USD 418.75**.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**The caller named exactly one problem: stop the project and settle it.** The visible corpus adds one
more, and no further one.

| # | Problem | Waits on | Direction | Order |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Settle the stopped project (the caller's own write) | B | A waits on B | second |
| B | Raise the storage charge on the project (the office's own write) | — | root of the chain | first |

**Hop A → B, reasoning chain, marked `state-derived`.**

1. The document governing what the caller asked for is `Settlement of a Retrofit Project the Owner
   Stops` (`settlement_of_a_project_the_owner_stops_387d807d.json`). Its own rule carries the sentence:
   > "The settlement figure on a stopped project is worked out only once every week the delivered
   > equipment has stood in storage is carried as a storage charge on the project's billing record."

   This is a **state-form** sentence with an ordering connective ("only once"). It names a
   record-visible state — a storage charge standing on the project's billing record covering every week
   the equipment has stood in storage — and names no action, no performer, no tool and no other document.
2. **Does the state hold?** `find_retrofit_events(project_id='4ca039dc-…')` returns exactly three
   billing lines: a `deposit` billing, a `late_fee` billing and (separately) a payment and a change
   allowance credit. **No storage line stands on the record.** Yet two deliveries are recorded
   `stored_off_site: 'stored'` (`DL-880655` and `DL-880656`, 2026-04-22), so weeks have stood in storage
   that are not carried. The state does **not** hold.
3. **Which write brings the state about?** Searching the corpus with the words the records themselves
   use — `stored`, `storage`, "a building cannot receive" — reaches `Storage Billing on Equipment a
   Building Cannot Yet Receive` (`storage_billing_on_equipment_a_site_cannot_receive_6948fd82.json`),
   whose own rule describes precisely that write: "A storage charge is raised as a billing line on the
   project it belongs to. Raising it adds a storage line to the project's record entries, dated the day
   it is raised, and the amount owed on the project rises by the same amount." That document names its
   own tool in its own invocation block (`bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e`) and nothing else.
   I reached it from the records' vocabulary, not from any wording borrowed out of the settlement
   document, and the settlement document names neither that tool nor that document.
4. The amount of that write is fixed by `Computation of the Storage Charge on a Retrofit Project`,
   reached from the same words. Item 4a gives USD 517.50.
5. Once the storage line stands, the state the sentence names holds, and the settlement figure can be
   worked out — and the storage billing is itself one of "the deposit, mobilisation, progress, change
   order, storage and completion billings raised on the project" that the settlement computation counts,
   which is why the order is not merely formal: settling first would give a different, lower figure.

**No further hop.** The storage-billing document's own rule carries no prerequisite sentence, so the
chain terminates at B. No other document of the corpus states any waiting condition on either problem.

**Hop marks.** A → B: **state-derived**. No hop in this task was `action-named`, and **no hop was
pre-solved**: nowhere in the settlement document (or any other) is `bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e`
named, nor the storage problem, nor a route, nor an ordered step list crossing the two problems.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every figure in item 4 rests on a quoted
document sentence plus a quoted query return; nothing required a hidden field.

**The closest alternative at each boundary, and the visible sentence or record that excludes it:**

| Boundary | Closest alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|---|
| storage clock start | the arrival day, 2026-04-22 | `The Day from Which Storage Runs…`: arrival earlier than the booked day **and** a booked day already past → "the booked installation day, rather than the arrival day"; records give 2026-04-22 < 2026-06-01 < 2026-06-18 |
| free period | 1 week (no agreement) or 3 weeks (agreement, no late fee) | `find_maintenance_agreements` → PMA at Kestrel Court `status 'active'` excludes 1 week; late-fee line due 2026-04-18 inside the twelve months excludes 3 weeks |
| weekly storage rate | the bare class rate USD 225, or the rack premium USD 45 | most recent **stored** delivery is `equipment_type 'chiller'`; the rack tier lists "air handler, makeup air unit, VRF system" only |
| weekly charge for the lot | the rate as it stands (one unit), or rate × 2 | exactly **two** deliveries carry `stored_off_site 'stored'`; "Two units come to one and a half bays rather than two" |
| stage | after mobilisation (55 %), or after award (8 %) | `mobilization_date ''` excludes the first; `equipment_released_date '2026-02-20'` excludes the third |
| notice relief | 50 per cent, or the full rate | notice_date 2026-06-09 is **after** the booked day 2026-06-01, not "more than 30 days before" it; and a confirmed notice does stand, so the full rate is excluded |
| equipment share | 50 per cent (baseline) or 55 per cent | the most recent delivery is a chiller, which the 65 per cent tier names |
| restocking fee | the bare class 20 per cent | 2026-04-22 to 2026-06-18 is 57 days, "30 days or more" |
| late fees carried | the whole 837.50, or nothing | exactly one late fee line stands → the 50 per cent tier |
| credits issued | counting the USD 13400 `retrofit_change_allowance_credited` line as a credit against the settlement | `Article on Changes to the Contracted Scope`, clause 1: "The allowance is never refunded if it goes unused, because it is an authority to spend and not a deposit." The change allowance is an authority to spend, not a credit issued on the account; `find_retrofit_events` also records it under a different entry kind from a credit issued, and `find_retrofit_projects` still shows `change_allowance_remaining 13400.0` |
| object | the closed Equipment Replacement Order at Halstead Commons | different building, different scope, `status 'closed'`; "Nothing is pooled between projects" |
| owner of the stop | the agent stopping the project | `Settlement of a Retrofit Project the Owner Stops`: "Stopping the project is the owner's own act… the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it"; and the caller: "she will do the stopping herself" |
| terminal action | a handoff to a human | no visible dead-end ground applies; the corpus states a complete basis for stopping and settling |

**Counter-proof against "do only the one thing the customer asked for".**
If the agent simply unlocked `settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f` and had the caller stop the project
without first raising the storage charge, the result would violate a visible principle, not merely
produce a smaller number: the settlement document's own rule says the figure "is worked out **only
once** every week the delivered equipment has stood in storage is carried as a storage charge on the
project's billing record", and the records show two stored deliveries standing since 2026-04-22 with
no storage line on the billing record. The figure would therefore not yet be fixed at all; and because
the settlement computation counts "storage" among the billings it sums, the figure reached would be
USD 517.50 short. The wrong answer is excluded by a visible sentence plus a visible record, **without**
any document naming the storage tool, the storage problem or a route.

**Counter-proof on the calculation: the fall-back numbers with no factor applied.**
Reading only the computation document plus the product figures it names, and applying no factor:

- Storage charge: clock from the arrival day 2026-04-22; 57 days → 9 whole weeks begun; free period
  1 week (baseline step 3) → 8 weeks charged; weekly storage rate = the class's USD 225 (from
  `Equipment Lead Times, Storage, Temporary Cooling and After-Hours Charges`); weekly charge for the lot
  = "the weekly storage rate as it stands" → **USD 1800.00**. Definite, and different from USD 517.50.
- Settlement figure: stage "after award and before the equipment order was released" (baseline) → 8 per
  cent of 268000 = 21440.00; equipment value at 50 per cent = 134000.00; restocking at the class's
  20 per cent = 26800.00; billings counted 67000.00 + the storage line; late fees "in full" 837.50;
  less payments 67000.00 → **definite**, and different from USD 103446.25.

Both fall-backs are computable and definite, so neither computation document is under-specified; and
each differs from the answer reached, so every factor I applied bears weight.
